name: Galvanic Marrow Projector GMP-1 'Marrowbone'
description:
The Galvanic Marrow Projector GMP-1 delivers a precisely tuned galvanic current through a directional conductive beam that penetrates surface tissue and targets the high-conductivity environment of bone marrow directly. Bone marrow, suspended in its semi-fluid lipid matrix within the skeletal cavity, conducts galvanic current far more readily than surrounding tissue, allowing the GMP-1 to bypass surface armor and even subdermal plating by routing its effect through the skeletal system rather than against it. The result is an intense, incapacitating pain response originating from deep within the body, accompanied by temporary disruption of the hematopoietic activity that marrow performs — effectively stunning the body's blood production system.

Ringo Corponation developed the GMP-1 for crowd compliance applications following regulatory pressure against lethal crowd control options after the GLMZ South Quarter incident. The weapon was marketed as a 'non-lethal deep compliance system' — language that has since been challenged in three separate regulatory reviews, as prolonged exposure causes marrow necrosis and long-term hematological complications that manifest weeks after the initial event. Ringo's legal team has successfully argued that these delayed complications do not constitute immediate lethality, keeping the weapon in a compliance classification rather than a lethal one.

The GMP-1 fires with a low electrical buzz and leaves no visible wound on the target, which made it attractive to security forces wanting deniable compliance options. Users who have been hit describe the sensation as a profound wrongness centered in their bones — not surface pain but something deeper and more disorienting, as if the pain is coming from the inside of the body rather than the outside. The psychological effect is significant and persistent; many survivors report bone-deep anxiety responses for months afterward, triggered by the sound of electrical equipment.
legality: Licensed — certified compliance and security use; Restricted — extended exposure modification; Prohibited — civilian ownership
specifications:
effective range: 2–20 meters
current delivery: 0.4–2.8 mA adjustable, directed beam
exposure threshold safe: Under 3 seconds continuous
exposure threshold damaging: Over 8 seconds continuous
power source: Galvanic cell pack, 45 shots per charge at standard setting
weight: 2.6 kg
penetration depth: Effective against subdermal plating up to 8mm
form factor: Compact rifle with adjustable exposure dial and beam collimator
tactical_use: Used in crowd dispersal, detainee compliance, and situations requiring incapacitation without visible injury. Operators are trained to use short exposure bursts to induce compliance without crossing into tissue damage thresholds — though field reports consistently show operators exceeding safe exposure durations during high-stress deployments. The weapon's ability to penetrate subdermal armor makes it effective against heavily augmented targets who have otherwise made themselves resistant to surface-level compliance tools. In extended exposure configurations, used as a slow-acting punishment weapon whose effects are deniable due to the delayed onset of damage.
cultural_context: The GMP-1 is one of GLMZ's most politically contested weapons. Compliance forces defend it as a non-lethal option that saves lives; medical researchers and civil rights organizations have spent years documenting the delayed hematological damage that Ringo Corponation's legal team continues to reframe as unrelated health conditions. The weapon has become a symbol of institutional violence that hides behind technicality — the slow ache that the city produces in the people it controls. 'Marrowboned' has entered GLMZ slang as a term for someone whose resistance has been broken from the inside, left standing but fundamentally damaged.
known_users: GLMZ Compliance Authority crowd control units
Private prison contractors operating in the lower districts
'Patience' — a compliance specialist known for methodical, deniable interrogation work
story_hooks: A LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS researcher has quietly been treating an unusual cluster of hematological cases in the lower districts — all with the same damage profile, all claiming they were 'never hit by anything' — and the data is about to go public unless someone stops it.

A player character has been experiencing bone-deep aches for weeks after a crowd compliance incident — a street doctor tells them they have GMP-1 marrow damage, and the statute of limitations on filing a complaint expires in 72 hours.
A modified GMP-1 with the safety limiters removed has been used in a string of apparent natural deaths — the bodies show no external wounds, and the coroner is classifying them as cardiac events.

RINGO CORPONATION is lobbying to remove the exposure duration limits from the GMP-1's compliance classification — a player character is approached by a civil rights organization to steal the internal research documents that would prove the company already knows the current limits are insufficient.
related_entities: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Hematic Sentinel Array — 'The Warden'

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular rifle with a distinctly medical aesthetic corrupted by tactical brutalism. The form reads as precision instrument rather than traditional firearm—sleek, almost surgical in its lines, with an unsettling clinical coldness. The silhouette is narrow and purposeful, suggesting something designed to violate rather than defend.
physical_description.dimensions: 112 cm length overall; 8 cm width at widest point; 6.5 cm height including collimator assembly. Barrel section 34 cm, tapering gradually to a fine conductive emitter tip.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light in hand at 2.6 kg—lighter than expected for its length, creating an almost eerie weightlessness that belies its capacity for harm. Balanced forward toward the emitter, encouraging natural aim at vital zones.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade aluminum composite frame with integrated piezoelectric ceramic pockets embedded throughout the body. Conductive pathways threaded through structural members in visible microchannel grooving.
physical_description.finish: Brushed satin silver with oxidized copper accent striping along the energy channels. The finish is deliberately clinical and sterile, occasionally interrupted by microscopic burn marks from galvanic feedback. Appears polished but shows heat-stress discoloration in use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Metallic silver-gray primary with oxidized copper accent lines tracing the galvanic pathways. RINGO branding in medical-grade white. Dark polymer endcaps and grip in charcoal-black.
physical_description.grip_texture: Thermally-treated polymer grip with microscopic diamond-pattern texturing—designed to shed sweat and maintain contact during high-stress use. Slightly warm to the touch, conducting minor residual charge that creates subtle tingling against bare skin.
distinctive_features: Adjustable exposure dial (0.4–2.8 mA) mounted on the left side with numbered severity gradations and a haunting medical-aesthetic scale
Conductive beam collimator at the muzzle—a series of nested ceramic rings that glow faintly under operation
Visible microchannel grooves running the length of the frame in a web-like pattern that suggest internal current pathways
Three small piezoelectric impact sensors spaced along the barrel, flush-mounted and ringed with copper contact points
Galvanic cell pack housing recessed into the stock, transparent polymer window showing the blue-tinted electrolytic fluid within
Low-profile charging port disguised as a cosmetic seam on the rear endcap
No traditional safety mechanism—instead, an encrypted biometric trigger pad that glows soft amber when armed
Faint etched serial number and regulatory compliance stamps arranged in a deliberately clinical font
Heat vents along the upper receiver designed to resemble medical equipment rather than weapons
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: RINGO CORPONATION logo (stylized R enclosing a sine wave) laser-etched in white onto the left side of the lower receiver. Below it: 'GALVANIC MARROW PROJECTOR GMP-1' in sans-serif type. Serial plate mounted on the stock with compliance certification stamps. Model number and manufacturing date rendered in tiny white text beside the galvanic cell window.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-deployed units show burnishing on grip surfaces from gloved use, faint scorch marks around the collimator from electrical creep, and wear on the exposure dial from frequent adjustment. The aluminum shows minor stress micro-fractures in the channel grooves. Copper accent lines oxidize unevenly in use, creating a mottled patina that suggests the weapon has been actively firing. Many units show custom grip wraps or electrical tape modifications applied by field operators attempting to insulate against feedback, suggesting user discomfort with the weapon's residual conductivity.

image_prompt: Product photography of the Galvanic Marrow Projector GMP-1 'Marrowbone' displayed horizontally on a glossy obsidian surface, dramatically lit from the upper left with cool 5000K side-lighting that casts sharp shadows emphasizing the conductive channel grooves. A gloved tactical hand (black neoprene with copper contact pads visible) grips the stock. The aluminum frame reflects electric blue accent light along the pathway tracings. Extreme close-up detail on the ceramic collimator emitter tip, which glows with faint bioluminescent blue. Background is deep charcoal cyberpunk aesthetic with soft hex-grid projection mapping barely visible. The weapon's medical instrument design contrasts with tactical brutality. Sharp focus on the exposure dial showing numerical severity markings. The transparent galvanic cell window reveals swirling electrolytic fluid with suspended metallic particulates.
